content: Post-bariatric surgery hypoglycemia (PBSH) is a condition that occurs after bariatric surgery and is primarily caused by rapid gastric emptying. This rapid emptying of the stomach leads to the swift absorption of glucose into the bloodstream. As a result, there is an exaggerated release of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and other gastrointestinal hormones, which in turn triggers an excessive release of insulin. The symptoms of PBSH typically manifest 1 to 3 hours after consuming a meal high in carbohydrates. These symptoms include sweating, tremors, a rapid heart rate, intense hunger, confusion, seizures, and, in some cases, loss of consciousness. It is important to distinguish PBSH from dumping syndrome. Dumping syndrome occurs shortly after eating and tends to improve over time. In contrast, PBSH can persist or even emerge more than a year after the surgery.
